references.text: The Nazirite vow included abstinence from wine and strong drink, which provides the background for John's ascetic lifestyle mentioned in Luke 7:33.
Matthew describes John the Baptist's simple lifestyle with locusts and wild honey as food, corresponding to the description in Luke 7:33 that he ate no bread and drank no wine.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says the same thing: that John came neither eating nor drinking, and people said he had a demon.
Mark's description of John's simple way of life in the wilderness confirms the ascetic lifestyle mentioned in Luke 7:33.
The angel's prophecy about John before his birth, stating that he should not drink wine or strong drink – this is the fulfillment of what is now criticized in Luke 7:33.
The next verse provides the contrast: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, yet he too was criticized – showing that the people rejected both John's asceticism and Jesus' participation in meals.
The accusation that someone had a demon was also directed at Jesus himself, just as it was directed here against John – a pattern of rejection through demonization.
The crowd accused Jesus of having a demon, just as John was accused in Luke 7:33. Both were rejected with charges of demonic possession.
